# Guide-only Git-read adoption trial

An independent agent used only the candidate README, CUE schema and binary help.
It created an owned synthetic ordinary repository with fictitious identity and
protected sibling controls. No implementation/test source, real history, network,
provider, hook installation or global configuration was used.

Initial status, immutable diff and bounded history succeeded. A synthetic marked
path blocked with exit 1/rule/zero rows; missing required Git registration and a
wrong executable hash returned exit 2 before repository calls. The guide required
schema reading to reconstruct controls, and binary help omitted the Git profile.

The guide now supplies complete synthetic scope/policy/request controls, explicit
operator path/hash/version collection and topology limits. Both global help and
`git-inspect --help` list the profile and three request kinds without control files.
The reviewer copied those updated controls, substituted its private registered values,
and reran the final binary identified in [README](README.md):

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| Status | Exit 0/ok, two selected rows |
| History, maxCommits=1 | Exit 0/ok, one row, explicit hasMore |
| Immutable base OID to HEAD diff | Exit 0/ok, one change |
| Global/subcommand help | Exit 0, profile and kinds discoverable |

The updated command-safety-audit skill passed skill-creator's validator using an
existing offline dependency environment. Manual routing review selected Git-read
adoption and hook-safety audit requests, excluding ordinary `git status` and prose
editing. This is written routing validation, not automatic activation on an installed
agent host. Other native hosts, linked/bare setup usability and attended production
task benefit remain outside this guide trial.
